msContents.summary: Royal oath taken by Thotomous, son of Harpaesis, to Praktor Euphronios. Promise of payment of the outstanding debts. Greek subscription with summary of content.

ὅρκος Θοτμώσιος Ἅρσιος (sic) ἱερογραμματέως
Ἀπόλλωνος πόλεως τῆς μεγάλης
περὶ τῶν ὀφειλημάτων, ὅπως
ἀγάγῃ εἰς ὁμόλογον

The oath which has taken Thotomous, son of Harpaesis, to
Euphronios, praktor of the temples,
in 23rd regnal year, 17th of Phamenoth.
The priest of (the god) Horus-son-of-Isis, priest of Ptah, priest of the Gods Euergetai
Thotomous, son of Harpaesis, is the one who speaks to Euphronios,
praktor [of the temples]: [I take an oath]
in the name of Pharaoh Ptolemaios (III.),
son of Ptolemaios (II.), and (in the name of) the Female Pharaoh
Berenike (II.) and (in the name of) the gods Adelphoi, (and in the name of) the gods Euergetai
and of Isis [and Serapis and] of all [gods]
of Egypt. I will hold a meeting in
the nome of Edfu, together with your attorneys.
The arrears, which I have recorded for you in those years
in which I should have collected them, according to that was was written for you
by the scribes (of) [your] attorneys,
those I will hand over to you together with the interest burdened(?) on them.
Provided that I shall take the oath above as a true
oath, I will be among those who are favored by Pharaoh.
If I will take it as a false one, I will be in punishment,
and I will not escape to
a place-of-oath (or) a place-of-protection.
Written in 23rd regnal year, 17th of Phamenoth.
Oath of Thotomous, son of Harpaesis, Hierogrammateus
from Edfou
concerning the obligations, so that
he fulfills them accordingly.
